title: Raw localization of the inverse integral scalar comparison and its three-field laws
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a noetherian finite-dimensional scheme $T$ with $\ell$ invertible. Use the integral and rational scalar systems and comparison presentations of [def-fd-raw-localization-scalar-data]. Let $I_E$ be the supplied exact integral stage identifications. Suppose $b_{L/E}:I_E C_{L/E}\cong U_{L/E}I_L$ commutes with the specified shifts, both endpoint composites are exact, ordinary transport is tensor-generator normalized, and b has the specified quotient-completion lift. Assume the integral inverse cocycle and the multiplication/completeness unit equation. Then there are a RationalFamily fixed by the supplied raw rational stage functors and their shifts, and natural isomorphisms $j_{L/E}:S_{L/E}J_L\cong J_EP_{L/E}$. Their hom and inverse commute with the specified shifts, their endpoint composites are exact, and on every localized integral object their hom is exactly the localization of $b_{L/E}^{-1}$ followed by the inverse ordinary-scalar localization comparison. At equal fields j is J of the framework scalar unit. The three-field equation is $j_{M/L}P_{M/L}(j_{L/E})a^p_{M,L,E}=J_M(a^s_{M,L,E})j_{M/E}$, in Lean composition order. Both unit substitutions hold with the specified framework unit maps. This conclusion stops at the three-field and unit equations; it asserts neither four-field contraction. All inclusions are non-strict, so repeated fields, zero objects and empty schemes are included.

proof.text: Use [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi, def-weil-pbc-rational-category, def-weil-linear-scalar-localization] for the raw Hom modules and their bilinear composition. For $E\subseteq L$, ordinary and strict-tower integral extension are additive and semilinear for $\mathcal O_E\to\mathcal O_L$: on an integral arrow $rf$, tensor extension sends the scalar $r$ to its image in $\mathcal O_L$, and quotient maps and the strict tower preserve this equality. The image of $\varpi_E$ is a unit in $L=\mathcal O_L[1/\varpi_L]$, since it is a nonzero element of the subfield $E$. Thus [lem-pur-semilinear-scalar-localization] applies to both extensions, the identity identifications and their composites. Their localized functors are the specified ones: $S_{L/E}$ is integral strict-tower extension followed by rationalization [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], and $P_{L/E}$ is the rationalization of the constructible restriction of $C_{L/E}$ [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension]; on every generator $f\otimes x$ the extension formula is $F(f)\otimes x$, using $E\subseteq L$, and $J$ fixes that generator. Consequently the localization of $b^{-1}:U_{L/E}\to C_{L/E}$ has source $J_LS_{L/E}$ and target $P_{L/E}J_E$. The lemma gives the exact natural isomorphism $j_{L/E,K}=Q_L(b_{L/E,K}^{-1})$, its inverse $Q_L(b_{L/E,K})$, and compatibility with the specified shifts. The lift is precisely the given inverse quotient-map lift: this construction applies $Q_L$ to that map itself and makes no replacement of it. All objects of a raw localization are integral objects, so this defines every component.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-semilinear-scalar-localization] to the assumed integral inverse equation, using final localization $Q_M$. It preserves vertical composition and both whiskerings, so its left side becomes $a^p_{M,L,E}\,P_{M/L}(j_{L/E})\,j_{M/L,S_{L/E}K}$ and its right side becomes $j_{M/E}\,J_M(a^s_{M,L,E})$. The identifications are fixed by Step 1 and by the hypothesis that $A^C,A^U$ rationalize to the specified $a^p,a^s$, respectively. This proves the required three-field equation with the stated arrow direction.

source.place: Final coefficient-category sentence; extraction Old steps 7–8: localization of the inverse cocycle and specified associator pentagons

proof.text: For equal fields, $j_{E/E,K}=Q_E(b_{E/E,K}^{-1})$ is the inverse of the assumed completeness unit after multiplication, in exactly the prescribed integral normalization. Apply [lem-pur-semilinear-scalar-localization] to both assumed multiplication/completeness unit substitutions in the integral inverse equation and to the integral scalar unit laws. The localized equations are the two rational unit squares: all components are the localized original unit components, with the scalar functors identified in Step 1. This proves both unit equations, without declaring a nonidentity integral completeness map to be the identity.
